subject: Follow-up: licensing cadence + $/1M token anchors for VPC rollout
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Marta Alvarez <marta@clarityhealth.io>, procurement@clarityhealth.io
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: licensing cadence + $/1M token anchors for VPC rollout

Hi Marta / Clarity procurement team,

Great to meet today — thanks for walking us through the architecture goals and compliance constraints. Short recap and a couple of asks so we can model a pricing sketch that matches your budget: 

Call recap (high level):
- Target initial usage: you mentioned pilot usage for the clinical assistant ~50–75k queries/day (roughly 12–18M tokens/month).
- Ramp expectations: product roadmap suggests 8–12x growth over 9–12 months if pilot is successful.
- Compliance: VPC-only deployment, HIPAA controls, KMS for key management, 3rd-party logging retention 12 months.
- Environments: you referenced prod + staging + sandbox; please confirm exact counts per team (we flagged env separation as a pricing knob).

Pricing/unit-econ anchors we discussed today:
- Licensing model options we can offer: (A) annual committed license + token overage; (B) per-environment subscription + metered token billing; (C) fully committed token pool across envs.
- Target unit-price we often use as an anchor for sizing conversations: $/1M tokens varies materially with committed volume and support band (pilot numbers are typically higher).

Immediate asks for our next pricing sketch:
1) Confirm expected month-1 committed tokens (best single number, e.g., 12M / 18M / 25M).
2) Confirm how many logical environments you need isolated billing/keys for (prod/staging/sandbox/uat/analytics).
3) Confirm preferred procurement cadence: monthly with annual PO, or annual prepay/commit?

I attached the worksheet you mentioned (clarity_requirements.xlsx) — I filled the env table and left the token ramp blank for you to populate. Once we have those three inputs we’ll produce 3 pricing scenarios (pilot, scale, enterprise) showing per-1M token economics and headcount/support inclusions.

Proposed next step: if you’re available, we can run a 60-minute pricing workshop with our solutions engineering + finance on Thursday (your timezone).

Thanks —
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: clarity_requirements.xlsx (worksheet: environments & token ramp)
From: Marta Alvarez <marta@clarityhealth.io>

Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 17:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: licensing cadence + $/1M token anchors for VPC rollout

Thanks, Logan — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Month-1 committed tokens: we expect to start ~15M tokens/month for the clinical assistant pilot (that reflects batch processing + interactive volumes).
- Ramp: we’re modeling a conservative 3x by month 6 and 8–10x by month 12 if adoption goes well (so ~45M month6 / ~150M month12 as directional).
- Environments: we need 4 logical envs isolated by keys (prod, staging, sandbox, analytics).
- Procurement cadence: preference is annual commitment (PO) with quarterly billing — open to discussing prepay discounts.
- Budget band: procurement has flagged $25k–$40k/month for the first 12 months (inclusive of support). We understand unit pricing will change as we commit to larger buckets.

Questions for Redwood:
- What is the Enterprise support band cost vs Standard (we assume Enterprise includes faster SLAs, runbooks, and quarterly reviews)?
- Can you sketch a 12-month scenario that shows monthly cost under annual commit vs month-to-month for 15M -> 150M ramp?

Happy to jump on the Thursday workshop — Marta (my calendar) is free after 11am PT.

Best,
Marta Alvarez
Head of Product Ops, Clarity Health
marta@clarityhealth.io | +1 (650) 555-4401
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Marta Alvarez <marta@clarityhealth.io>, procurement@clarityhealth.io
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: licensing cadence + $/1M token anchors for VPC rollout

Marta — thanks, that helps a lot. Based on the 15M starting point and the 4 envs requirement, I sketched three scenarios below to make the unit-econ tradeoffs explicit. These are illustrative and will be formalized after the workshop/worksheet.

Scenario A — Pilot (annual commit, conservative)
- Environments: 4 (prod/staging/sandbox/analytics)
- Commit: 50M tokens/year (~4.2M tokens/month average, but we price as a committed annual bucket)
- Base annual license (VPC private control plane + KMS + basic audit): $120,000/year (equivalent $10k/month)
- Included support: Standard (business hours, 48h escalation)
- Token overage / metered pricing above commit: $1,000 per 1M tokens
- Effective rate at 15M/month steady-state (if you moved to a 180M annualized consumption): example math shown in workshop; pilot pricing typically results in ~$900–$1,100 per 1M tokens once you include license amortization across tokens used.

Scenario B — Scale (recommended if you plan to ramp to ~150M/yr quickly)
- Environments: 4–6 (add staging/uat team)
- Commit: 200M tokens/year
- Base annual license: $360,000/year (includes higher throughput capacity & dedicated instance reservations)
- Included support: Enterprise Lite (priority queueing, 24/7 on-call for Sev1)
- Token overage price: $600 per 1M tokens above commit
- Effective unit: when amortized across committed volume, this scenario delivers ~ $480–$700 per 1M tokens depending on utilization and enabled optimizations (quantization, caching).

Scenario C — Enterprise (large commit + multi-env)
- Environments: 8–12 (teams + analytics + integration testing)
- Commit: 1B tokens/year
- Base annual license: $1,200,000/year (includes multi-region fallback, extended retention, SOC2 evidence packaging)
- Included support: Enterprise (dedicated TAM, weekly operational reviews)
- Token overage price: $360 per 1M tokens above commit
- Effective unit: ~$360/1M tokens at scale.

Notes: these figures are directional to give procurement anchors. Key levers that change the $/1M token: committed volume, environment count (isolated envs require additional license seats), support band, and enabled optimizations (intelligent caching, 8-bit quantization, and prefix caching can materially reduce effective tokens billed).

Attachments: I’m attaching a short pricing sketch (redwood_private_pricing_v1.pdf) that converts these scenarios into monthly cashflows so procurement can map to their $25k–$40k band.

Proposed next steps:
1) Workshop on Thursday at 11:30am PT with our solutions + finance to finalize the worksheet and pick a scenario.
2) Post-workshop we’ll produce a formal commercial term sheet (license + support SOW + sample PO language).

If those scenarios look plausibly aligned, I’ll slot the workshop and loop in our finance lead for the commercial modeling.

Thanks —
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood_private_pricing_v1.pdf (pricing sketch)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: licensing cadence + $/1M token anchors for VPC rollout

Marta / team — quick technical notes to support the pricing scenarios above:

- Quantization + runtime: moving inference to 8-bit quantized models (where feasible) typically lowers per-token compute by ~25–40% and is one of the fastest levers to improve unit economics. We’ll validate model compatibility during the pilot.
- Caching: prefix and session KV cache reduces repeated token generation for multi-turn flows. For the clinical assistant this can reduce billed tokens by ~15–30% depending on prompt architecture.
- Environment isolation: each isolated env with its own KMS keys and audit logs increases operational overhead and a small per-env license surcharge (we modeled that into the base license numbers above).
- Support tiers: Enterprise includes 1h initial oncall response for Sev1 and a named TAM; Enterprise Lite is 4h for Sev1. We’ll include the SLA table in the term sheet.

I can run a short tech session during the Thursday workshop to walk through caching, batching, and quantization options and the likely impact on the $/1M token numbers.

Cheers,
Evelyn Hart
Solutions Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com
